profile.name: Rohan Marar
profile.role: AI Engineer. Robotics researcher. Author. Lifelong homelabber.
profile.headline: Curious about intelligence. Driven to build.
profile.intro: I work across artificial intelligence, robotics, and the systems that bring ideas to life. Currently pursuing an M.S. in Artificial Intelligence at the University at Buffalo, and contributing to research at DRONESLab.
profile.about:
I like understanding complex systems from first principles, then building something useful with what I learn. My interests span deep learning, robotic perception, reinforcement learning, and self-hosted infrastructure.

At UB's DRONESLab, I volunteer on active illumination for Boston Dynamics Spot, supporting data collection in challenging lighting conditions and exploring 3D reconstruction workflows.

Outside engineering, I write books, lift weights, cook, and think far too much about films. This site is a record of the things I build and the questions that keep me curious.
profile.education: M.S. Artificial Intelligence · University at Buffalo

projects.title: Active illumination for Spot
projects.summary: Exploring how lighting affects robotic perception, through low-light data collection and 3D reconstruction workflows at UB's DRONESLab.
projects.body:
Reliable perception becomes harder when a robot moves through dark corridors, reflective surfaces, and uneven lighting. I contribute to an active illumination project for Boston Dynamics Spot at the University at Buffalo.

My work includes operating Spot during data collection and exploring a reconstruction pipeline from recorded imagery through COLMAP and GenRecon. The longer-term direction is a library of reconstructed environments for studying robotic perception under changing illumination.

This is ongoing work. Reconstruction quality and material realism remain areas to improve.
projects.stack: Boston Dynamics Spot, COLMAP, GenRecon, Blender

projects.title: Cadence
projects.summary: A personalized research-paper discovery platform: semantic recommendations, a swipe-based feed, and a cross-platform PWA.
projects.body:
I designed and built Cadence as a full-stack research discovery app, with the idea of making research discovery feel as personal as a music feed.

I fine-tuned SPECTER2 on a corpus of 2.28 million research papers across computer science, physics, biology, medicine, mathematics, and economics, generating 768-dimensional embeddings. A usearch vector index and interaction-weighted taste vectors power a personalized feed, with recency decay and sub-300 ms feed generation.

The ingestion pipeline pulls more than 500 new papers daily from arXiv and bioRxiv, embeds them on my local RTX 4060 Ti, and hot-reloads the live index.

I built a FastAPI backend with JWT authentication and Supabase PostgreSQL, and a React Native + Expo frontend exported as an installable PWA. It includes swipe-based discovery, personalized sections, open-access PDF reading, reading streaks, saved libraries, playlists, and an eight-step onboarding flow.

I handled the full stack: model fine-tuning, ingestion, recommendation logic, API, frontend, infrastructure, and deployment.
projects.stack: SPECTER2, usearch, FastAPI, Supabase, React Native, Expo

projects.title: WatcherML
projects.summary: A local-first Python SDK and CLI for recording reproducible ML runs, investigating failures, and verifying bounded recovery.
projects.body:
I built WatcherML as a pip-installable Python SDK and command-line tool for recording configurations, artifacts, model state, and failure conditions.

It captures reproducible training runs and packages failure evidence into deterministic capsules. Recovery campaigns make failed experiments easier to reproduce, analyze, and recover under explicit compute and quality constraints.

Local SQLite storage and portable artifacts keep the evidence close to the experiment. The current published package focuses on recorded evidence, deterministic failure classification, controlled CUDA out-of-memory interventions, and independent confirmation of a recovery.

Install the package with: pip install watcherml
projects.stack: Python, SQLite, PyTorch, CLI, experiment tracking

projects.title: Bulkbites
projects.summary: An Android nutrition app combining custom food recognition models, meal planning, and fitness tracking.
projects.body:
I co-founded Tensorbuilds with Prathmesh Gawali and built Bulkbites, an AI-powered nutrition app for Android.

I developed custom computer vision models to identify more than 260 foods, and built the mobile app in React Native. The PyTorch models were deployed on an Ubuntu virtual machine in Oracle Cloud.

The app brings together food logging, micronutrient information, barcode scanning, meal planning, weight tracking, and workout summaries.
projects.stack: PyTorch, React Native, Python, Oracle Cloud

projects.title: A home for my infrastructure
projects.summary: A personal Linux homelab for self-hosted services, development, observability, and home automation.
projects.body:
My homelab is where I learn by running real systems. It has evolved from experiments with Proxmox and virtual machines into a Linux workstation running Docker-based services.

I use it for development, self-hosted tools, monitoring, and Home Assistant. Working with reverse proxies, Cloudflare tunnels, containers, and backups has made infrastructure a hands-on part of my engineering practice.

Recent work includes room-temperature sensors built with ESP8266 boards and BME280 sensors, connected to Home Assistant and a Z-Wave thermostat.
projects.stack: Ubuntu, Docker, Home Assistant, ESPHome, Z-Wave

projects.title: Object detection with YOLO-NAS
projects.summary: Transfer learning experiments with pretrained object detectors, custom datasets, and iterative fine-tuning.
projects.body:
A computer vision project exploring how pretrained object detection models can be adapted to a custom dataset.

I ran experiments with fine-tuning techniques and documented the training approach and results in the repository's technical report.

other.title: TensorBuilds
other.description:
My first attempt at building and running an unofficial startup began during college. I experimented with Wealthify, a financial forecasting web service, and later worked with my co-founder Prathmesh Gawali on InfraEdge, a hosting service running on our own Linux infrastructure.

We eventually focused on Bulkbites, an AI-powered nutrition app for Android. I built custom food recognition models and the React Native app, while learning about deployment, marketing, outreach, and bringing an idea to real users.

I later handed over my code and app access to my co-founder before moving to the United States. The experience shaped how I approach building products.
